questions.prompt: What are the three types of muscle?
questions.explanation: The body has three muscle types: skeletal (body movement), smooth (organs), and cardiac (heart).
questions.misconception: The three types are named by where they work, not by color or speed.

questions.prompt: How does a muscle make your body move?
options: It contracts (shortens) and pulls on a bone
questions.explanation: A muscle shortens (contracts), pulling on the bone it is attached to, which moves the joint.
questions.misconception: Muscles only pull, they never push - that is why they work in pairs.

questions.prompt: Which muscle type is only in the heart and beats automatically?
questions.explanation: Cardiac muscle is found only in the heart, beats automatically, and never tires.
questions.misconception: Skeletal muscle is voluntary and smooth muscle is in organs - only the heart has cardiac muscle.

questions.prompt: Why do muscles often work in pairs?
options: One pulls one way and the other pulls back
So they can both be idle
questions.explanation: Because muscles only pull, one muscle pulls the limb one way and its partner pulls it back - pairs make joints move both ways.
questions.misconception: Pairs are not about looks or sharing - they exist because muscles can only contract and pull.

questions.prompt: Why do you get tired and breathe faster during exercise?
options: Working muscles use extra energy and oxygen
questions.explanation: Hard-working muscles burn extra energy and need more oxygen, so you breathe faster to supply them.
questions.misconception: It's about energy supply to the muscles, not bones, skin, or ears.
